work.heading: Recent work
work.subheading: Four live projects across esports, luxury fashion, e-commerce, and fragrance.

imperfect.name: IMPerfect Gaming
imperfect.description: Puerto Rico org competing in OW2 & Marvel Rivals
imperfect.challenge: Building a bilingual org management system that could handle roster moves, scrim scheduling, and team announcements — all without requiring the coaching staff to touch the codebase. The solution was a role-based Team Hub with scoped permissions for Admin, Coach, and Manager roles.

emmalina.name: Emmalina
emmalina.description: Personal stylist brand for a Saks/NM/Bergdorf associate
emmalina.challenge: The client needed to convert casual site visitors into private styling clients, while simultaneously driving affiliate sales through Saks, Neiman Marcus, and Bergdorf Goodman. We restructured the site around her personal brand first, with affiliate commerce as a secondary layer — not the other way around.

magenta.name: Magenta The Label
magenta.challenge: Launching a Shopify store for a handcrafted product brand where every item is one-of-a-kind created a unique inventory problem — standard e-commerce flows assume repeatable SKUs. We built a custom product structure that communicated scarcity as a feature, not a limitation, which directly improved conversion.

profumo.name: Profumo di Vita
profumo.description: Bilingual luxury fragrance store, 2 PR locations
profumo.challenge: Operating as a fully bilingual EN/ES store with two physical Puerto Rico locations meant every piece of content — product descriptions, membership tier details, store hours, promotional copy — had to be maintained in parallel without creating double the workload. We implemented a translation management system that kept both languages in sync with a single content update.

about.heading: Who's behind this
about.p1: I'm John Vincent, a web designer and digital strategist based in Puerto Rico. I started building websites for local businesses and organizations because I saw a gap — great businesses with weak digital presence, and agencies charging way too much to fix it.
about.p2: I use AI-assisted workflows to move faster and smarter than a traditional agency, without cutting corners on quality. Every project I take on gets my full attention — not a junior designer or an outsourced team.
about.p3: Every site I build meets WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards and ships fully bilingual in English and Puerto Rico Spanish — not machine-translated. These aren't add-ons. They're how the work gets done.
about.p4: My clients range from esports organizations to luxury fashion stylists to fragrance retailers. What they have in common: they needed a digital presence that performs, and they wanted someone who actually gets their business.

checker.metaDescription: Paste your website address and get a quick, honest accessibility check in seconds. Free, in English and Spanish.
checker.title: Free website accessibility check
checker.dek: Paste your website address. In a few seconds you get a short, honest list of problems that can stop people from using your site.

form.label: Your website address
form.hint: We check the one page you type. We do not save it.
form.checking: Checking the page. This usually takes under 15 seconds.

errors.invalid_url: That does not look like a website address. Try something like yoursite.com.
errors.blocked: We can only check public websites.
errors.unreachable: We could not open that page. Check the address. Some sites also block automatic checks.
errors.timeout: The site took too long to answer. Please try again in a minute.
errors.too_large: That page is too big for the quick check.
errors.too_complex: This page is too big for the quick check. A full audit can check it by hand.
errors.not_html: That address is not a web page. It may be a file or an image.
errors.rate_limited: You have run a few checks already. Please wait 10 minutes and try again.
errors.busy: The quick check is busy right now. Please try again in a few minutes.
errors.scan_failed: Something went wrong on our side. Please try again.

result.heading: Quick check for {page}
result.none: The quick check found no problems on this page. That is a good start, but a quick check cannot see everything. See the list below.
result.found: We found {problems, plural, one {# kind of problem} other {# kinds of problems}} in {places, plural, one {# place} other {# places}} on this page.
result.byImpactHeading: Problems by how much they get in the way
result.topHeading: {count, plural, one {The problem to fix first} other {The # problems to fix first}}
result.thin: This page has very little text in its code. If it fills in its content with JavaScript after it loads, the quick check could not see that part, so the real list may be longer.

critical.name: Critical
critical.help: Can stop some people from using the page at all

serious.name: Serious
serious.help: Makes the page very hard to use for some people

moderate.name: Moderate
moderate.help: Gets in the way and slows people down

note.heading: This is a quick check, not a full audit
note.body: It reads the page code as your server first sends it, before any scripts run. Automated checks find only part of the problems. A full audit tests the rest by hand.
note.cannotHeading: What the quick check cannot see
cannot: Color contrast, like text too faint to read
How the page looks and works on a phone
Using the page with only a keyboard
How a screen reader reads the page out loud
Content added by JavaScript after the page loads

lead.heading: Want the full audit?
lead.body: Leave your email and John Vincent Digital will contact you about a full accessibility audit of your site, checked by hand, in English or Spanish.
lead.bodyAfterError: We can still check it by hand. Leave your email and John Vincent Digital will contact you about a full accessibility audit.
lead.success: We got it. John Vincent Digital will email you about your site soon.
lead.error: We could not send it. Please try again, or write to us on WhatsApp.
lead.privacy: We use your email only to reply about your site. It is sent through our form service, Formspree. No newsletter, no sharing.

rules.image-alt: Some images have no text description, so people who use a screen reader do not know what they show.
rules.input-image-alt: Some image buttons have no text, so a screen reader cannot say what they do.
rules.role-img-alt: Some elements act as images but have no text description.
rules.svg-img-alt: Some icons or graphics marked as images have no text description.
rules.area-alt: Some clickable areas on an image map have no text, so people cannot tell where they go.
rules.object-alt: Some embedded objects have no text description.
rules.link-name: Some links have no words a screen reader can read, so people cannot tell where they go.
rules.button-name: Some buttons have no name, so people who cannot see them do not know what they do.
rules.input-button-name: Some form buttons have no text, so their purpose is unclear.
rules.label: Some form fields have no label, so people do not know what to type in them.
rules.select-name: Some dropdown menus have no label, so people do not know what they are choosing.
rules.form-field-multiple-labels: Some form fields have more than one label, which confuses screen readers.
rules.label-content-name-mismatch: Some buttons or links have a hidden name that does not match the words on screen, which breaks voice control.
rules.frame-title: Some embedded maps, videos or feeds have no title, so people cannot tell what they are.
rules.frame-title-unique: Several embedded frames share the same title, so people cannot tell them apart.
rules.frame-focusable-content: Embedded content cannot be reached with the keyboard.
rules.document-title: The page has no title, so browser tabs and search results show no clear name.
rules.html-has-lang: The page does not say what language it is in, so screen readers may read it with the wrong accent.
rules.html-lang-valid: The page's language code is not valid, so screen readers may read it wrong.
rules.valid-lang: Some parts of the page have a language code that is not valid.
rules.html-xml-lang-mismatch: The page declares two different languages that do not match.
rules.meta-viewport: The page blocks zooming on phones, so people with low vision cannot make text bigger.
rules.meta-refresh: The page reloads or moves on by itself, which can cut people off mid-read.
rules.list: Some lists are built wrong, so screen readers cannot count or move through them.
rules.listitem: Some list items are outside a list, which confuses screen readers.
rules.definition-list: Some definition lists are built wrong, which confuses screen readers.
rules.dlitem: Some definition terms are outside their list, which confuses screen readers.
rules.duplicate-id-aria: Two or more elements share an ID that labels use, so the wrong label can be read.
rules.nested-interactive: Some clickable items sit inside other clickable items, so keyboards and screen readers get stuck.
rules.bypass: There is no way to skip past the menu, so keyboard users must tab through it on every page.
rules.autocomplete-valid: Some form fields use autofill hints wrong, so phones cannot fill them in for people.
rules.blink: Some text blinks, which is hard to read and can be distracting.
rules.marquee: Some text scrolls by itself, which many people cannot read in time.
rules.server-side-image-map: An image map only works with a mouse.
rules.video-caption: Some videos have no captions, so people who are deaf or hard of hearing miss what is said.
rules.audio-caption: Audio has no text version, so people who are deaf miss what is said.
rules.no-autoplay-audio: Sound plays by itself, which drowns out screen readers.
rules.td-headers-attr: Some table cells point to headers that do not exist.
rules.td-has-header: Some large tables have cells with no header, so screen readers cannot say what each number means.
rules.th-has-data-cells: Some table headers do not label any cells.
rules.table-fake-caption: A table uses a regular cell as its title instead of a real caption.
rules.p-as-heading: Some text looks like a heading but is not marked as one, so screen readers skip it.
rules.summary-name: Some expandable sections have no name.
rules.avoid-inline-spacing: Text spacing is locked, so people cannot adjust it to read more easily.
rules.css-orientation-lock: The page only works in one screen direction on phones and tablets.
rules.aria-hidden-body: The whole page is hidden from screen readers.
rules.aria-hidden-focus: Some hidden items can still be reached with the keyboard, which confuses people.
rules.aria: Some accessibility labels in the code are used wrong, so screen readers may announce the wrong thing.
rules.other: Another problem that makes the page harder to use for people with disabilities.
